questions.question_text: A loan of $\$25\,000$ is repaid in equal monthly instalments over $5$ years ($60$ months) at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$). Find the monthly repayment, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Used simple interest $(25\,000 + 25\,000 \times 0.06 \times 5)/60$.
Divided principal by 60 without adding interest.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.

questions.question_text: Sarah can afford $\$850$ per month for a home improvement loan over $7$ years ($84$ months). The bank charges $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.004$). What is the maximum amount Sarah can borrow, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Multiplied monthly payment by 84 without discounting for interest.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.
Calculated the future value of an annuity instead of present value.

questions.question_text: An amount of $\$200\,000$ is borrowed at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$). How much higher is the monthly repayment for a $15$-year loan ($180$ months) compared to a $30$-year loan ($360$ months)?

options.why: Divided principal by the difference in months.
Reported the 15-year repayment instead of the difference.
Reported the 30-year repayment instead of the difference.

questions.question_text: A loan of $\$12\,000$ is repaid in equal quarterly instalments over $4$ years ($16$ quarters) at $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly ($r=0.02$). Find the quarterly repayment, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Divided principal by 16 quarters without including interest.
Used simple interest formula on the quarterly repayments.
Used the annual rate with the quarterly $n$.

questions.question_text: A borrower can make monthly repayments of $\$750$ on a car loan over $3$ years ($36$ months) at $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.006$). Find the maximum amount that can be borrowed, to the nearest dollar.

options.why: Multiplied repayment by 36 months without interest discounting.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.
Calculated the future value of an annuity instead of present value.

questions.question_text: Why does making fortnightly repayments rather than monthly repayments save significant money over the life of a home loan?

options.text: Making 26 fortnightly payments per year reduces the principal balance more frequently and is equivalent to making 13 monthly payments annually.
Fortnightly payments allow the bank to charge a lower interest rate automatically.
options.why: Mistakenly claims the quoted interest rate itself changes.

options.text: Simple interest applies instead of compound interest when paying fortnightly.
options.why: Claims interest model switches to simple interest.

options.text: Fortnightly repayments eliminate interest charges entirely in alternate fortnights.
options.why: Misunderstands the mechanics of compounding frequency.

questions.solution_text:
Paying fortnightly at half the monthly amount yields $26$ half-payments, which equals $13$ full monthly payments each year.
The extra annual repayment and more frequent balance reduction drastically reduce total interest.

questions.question_text: A personal loan of $\$30\,000$ at $13.3\%$ p.a. reducible interest is repaid in $10$ equal six-monthly instalments ($r=0.0665$). Find the exact repayment to the nearest cent, and state the balance $A_{10}$ if the repayment is rounded down to $\$4202$.

options.text: Repayment is $\$4202.48$; with $\$4202$ the remaining balance is $\$6.56$.
Repayment is $\$4202.00$; with $\$4202$ the remaining balance is $\$0.00$.
options.why: Assumed rounding to the dollar exactly pays off the loan.

options.text: Repayment is $\$4202.48$; with $\$4202$ the remaining balance is $-\$6.56$.
options.why: Inverted the sign of the remaining debt.

options.text: Repayment is $\$4202.48$; with $\$4202$ the remaining balance is $\$4.80$.
options.why: Multiplied rounding difference by 10 without compound growth.

questions.question_text: A mortgage of $\$240\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) is amortised over $20$ years ($M=\$1719.43$). If the monthly payment is increased to $\$2000$, the loan is paid off with $183$ full payments of $\$2000$ plus a final payment of $\$1432.84$. How much total interest is saved?

options.why: Assumed 184 full payments of $\$2000$ without adjusting for the smaller final payment.
Reported the new total interest paid instead of the interest saved.
Reported the total original interest instead of the savings.
